paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:9, he was a priest, and he, his sons and his wife were taken captive. They came before Rabbi Chanina, who did not accept them; they came before Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who accepted them.[^1][^2]

notes.text: “They were taken captive” is a verb, not the name of an additional person. The notice does not specify the legal scope of their acceptance.

The checked Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 2:9 names Chananyah Kartisaya, his sons and his wife as captives; Rabbi Chanina does not accept them, while Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi does. This supports the verbal reading of אישתבאי and the expansion of ריב״ל. Hyman additionally describes him as a priest; that word is not present in this checked paragraph. The notice’s legal scope and the place-name identification are not supplied.
